![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14272746/assets/d8452e497edc454ac0a71b4b5e9f00308ef7dbeb9c1413cc2bc82bbafb669b04.png)

A chemical is being poured into a conical vat at a constant rate of $18\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}\text{/h}.$ The vat has a radius of $10\,\text{m}$ at the wider end and a height of $10\,\text{m}.$ Find the rate of the liquid level increase at the moment when there is $9\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}$ of liquid in the vat. Do not round the answer.

The liquid level is increasing at a rate of
{{field-1}} $\text{m}/\text{h}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's consider the dimensions of the vat. Let's call $H=10\,\text{m}$ the height of the vat, and $R=10\,\text{m}$ its radius at the top. These quantities are fixed and do not change with time.

Now, let's consider the liquid level. We call $h$ the liquid level's height and $r$ the radius of the cone formed by the liquid. Both of these quantities, and the liquid volume $v,$ change with time. In particular, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=18\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}/\text{h},
$$

and we want to find $\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}$ when $v=9\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}.$

We need to find a relation between $h$ and the variable for which we know the rate of change, which is $v.$ This is given by the formula for the volume of a cone:

$$
v=\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h
$$

Before we differentiate the equation with respect to time, note that $r$ also appears in the formula. So, we need to simplify the formula by writing $r$ in terms of $h.$

Note that the cones formed by the vat and the liquid must be similar. Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{r}{h} & =\frac{R}{H} \\ \frac{r}{h} & =\frac{10}{10} \\ r & =h.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the volume formula as

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {r}^{2}h \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {(h)}^{2}h \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {h}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now that we have an equation relating $v$ and $h,$ we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}v & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{3}\pi {h}^{3}) \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} & =\pi {h}^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t}\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the rate at which the level of liquid in the vat is changing when $v=9\pi \,{\text{m}}^{3}.$ We can compute the value of $h$ at this moment as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9\pi  & =\frac{1}{3}\pi {h}^{3} \\ {h}^{3} & =27 \\ h & =3\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we plug in the known values into the formula for $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}$, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}18\pi  & =\pi (3)^{2}\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ 18 & =9\frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}h}{\text{d}t} & =2\,\text{m}/\text{h}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the liquid level is increasing at a rate of $2\,\text{m}/\text{h}.$
